findings.source_quote: ἀψευστὶ αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι αἰῶνι τὴν παράκλησιν ὑπισχνούμενος.
findings.english_quote: while unfailingly promising them consolation in the coming age.
findings.issue: ἀψευστὶ qualifies the promise as truthful or without falsehood. “Unfailingly promising” can instead describe the constancy of the act of promising and does not clearly preserve the assurance about its truthfulness.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “while truthfully promising them consolation in the coming age” or “while promising them, without falsehood, consolation in the coming age.” This proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τῆς διακρίσεως αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ σπεύδειν τοῦ ἀκούειν σπουδαιοτέρους πεποιηκυίας.
findings.english_quote: His delay had made them all the more eager to hurry to hear him.
findings.issue: A temporal interpretation through the sense of hesitation is possible, but the note inadequately represents the material alternatives. διάκρισις can concern discernment or judgment, and also dispute or discussion. The announced encounter with Simon makes the discussion/disputation reading particularly relevant. The crowd’s increased eagerness is compatible with delay, but does not itself distinguish that reading from these alternatives.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to preserve “his discernment/judgment” and “his discussion/disputation,” explicitly explaining that “delay” interprets a hesitation sense rather than an unambiguous temporal expression. Compare the main text with a candidate such as “his discussion had made them more eager to hasten to listen,” and explain the contextual choice. Neither that candidate nor the retained temporal rendering should be treated as newly accepted without fresh review. No correction or further verification of the printed Greek is required for this interpretive issue.

findings.source_quote: εἰ δὲ ταύτην λαβεῖν ὑμῶν τις μὴ θέλοι, τότε ἡμεῖς ἀποτιναξάμενοι εἰς μαρτυρίαν τῶν ποδῶν ἡμῶν τὸν ἐκ τῶν ὁδῶν κονιορτόν, ὃν διὰ τοὺς καμάτους βαστάζαντες ἠνέγκαμεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅπως σωθῆτε, εἰς ἑτέρων ἀπίωμεν οἰκίας καὶ πόλεις.
findings.english_quote: But if any one of you does not wish to receive it, then, after shaking from our feet as testimony the dust from the roads—which we carried through our exertions and brought to you so that you might be saved—let us depart for the houses and cities of others.
findings.issue: “Let us depart” treats ἀπίωμεν as an independent hortatory subjunctive. A substantial alternative is that it remains under the preceding ἵνα, alongside καταλάβῃ: the greeting is commanded so that peace may reach a receptive person and, in the contrary case, the messengers may depart. That syntactic connection is more directly preserved by “we may depart.” The draft does not disclose or explain its choice of an independent exhortation.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer a construction retaining the purpose-clause connection: “so that ... peace may take hold of him ... but if ... then we may, after shaking ... , depart for the houses and cities of others.” Alternatively, retain “let us depart” only with a note explaining the hortatory construal and preserving the dependent-purpose alternative. Any revised sentence requires fresh review; this is a syntactic interpretation issue, not evidence of print corruption.
